¶4 At the end of the book, he has written a chapter unnecessary. And this chapter that he has written as a main, all mystic, that's how someone who was not a mystic himself could have explained all these pages and stations of mystics himself. And some mystics say that actually Avicenna wrote this chapter, he himself was under the training of a businessman Abu Saeeed and he was in Riyadh himself. He was having those 40 nights or days of training and the way he has put The Stations of the Mystics, the title of the chapter which is very much well known as the ninth chapter of Al-Isharat wa’l-tanbihat. If you go through any book on mysticism, inevitably you will find an allusion to the ninth chapter of Al-Isharat wa’l-tanbihat which is about mystical stations.

¶5 He has explained very nicely and very understandingly how mystics progress through the station as we move up towards Allah. He has actually explained very nicely that first journey of the mystics which in annihilation or we call it arrival. Now of course, there are different explanations about asceticism and mysticism and devotion. If you come to page 85, chapter 7 of this section of the book, there is a remark concerning the first preparation. Of course, if someone just read through this, it's a bit confusing. It needs to be read somehow with some sort of reflection and someone having read the Arabic Book and some explanation of it as well. That's why I want to go a bit slowly through this chapter, probably during this session and next session inshallah.

¶6 And we find out how a mystic progresses through his or her journey towards God. So the first preparative stage willingness in the movement towards the truth. Of course this is called “Iradah”. That's the first line after the title iradah, which is willingness, the first step in the movement in that which they themselves hold an iradah ie willingness. This is the desire that overcomes the secret of insight. Secret of insight is Mureed of course, that's because they have a iradah so they're called Mureedun. You know that the one who desire is called a Mureed because they have an iradah. They are willing to do. Mureed is someone who's willing, so they have that willingness to go towards this path.

¶7 Now, of course this willingness doesn't come all of a sudden and this willingness is not in everyone known that billions of people live on this earth. And just very few of them would have that willingness to go towards Allah. How this willingness comes to the heart, he mentions here two issues. First by demonstrative certainty ie.Al Burhani Yaqini. They come by some sort of understanding and demonstration with high intellectual capacity, they come to the conclusion that yes, if they want prosperity and felicity they have to move towards Allah. So this iradah is certainly older or by tranquillity of the soul due to the confirmation of faith, Al aqdul al'iiman. Usually, of course, the first one of the demonstration of the intellect, it's very difficult.

¶8 Usually a person who for a long time who practices faith and does good action, gradually this willingness comes to the heart that this world is without value. I have to leave this and go towards Allah. That willingness is put in the heart by Allah and then gradually, they think that we have to wake up before dawn, we have to worship Allah we have to supplicate, communicate with him and they become very eager of worship. We have in many hades, that if god wants khair for that person, he would make worship pleasant for them. And this is when this iradah comes. They want to go towards Allah. So this is one of the best explanations of how a person sets forth on this path of mystical experience and mystical investigation, an iradah and Ibne Sina tries to show how this iradah is formed in a person because we don't find this iradah in many people.

¶9 Then in the next chapter, chapter eight, he said that now these two stages are preparatory stages, of course, we are not starting mystical experience yet. He says if that iradah comes, if someone wants to go towards Allah, then they need some training so that they make their soul agreeable to the world in which they want to enter, to which they want to connect because our souls are very much engrossed in the material life. It is not familiar with that type of life, that type of world. So they have to make some training, as for example, if he wants to become an athlete, you cannot go just like this. You need lots of training so that your body is prepared for it.

¶10 Now our soul is not prepared for those type experiences. There should be some training, so this training is called “Riyadah”. Riyadah is string and especially it comes from training of animals when they want us for example, to train a cow for ploughing or horse for hunting. They call this riyadah which is some sort of training and he said that the very word implies that you are like animals that should be trained so that you get to that station that the soul could go closer to Allah. So he says, furthermore that no one needs spiritual exercise but riyadah, is a spiritual exercise. Some people say this is self-mortification, I don't think this is self-mortification; it's just some training of the soul to become familiar with that other world, with the world of the malaqut in which they want to somehow go and come communicate.

¶11 With these kinds of exercises directs the soul towards 3 goals. So the aims of riyadah, he mentioned here, the first aim of riyadah is removing anything but haq out of the way. Now here, the first is to remove from the path of choice, whatever is other than the truth. This is one of the most difficult path. You have to somehow empty your soul from other needs. And that's when this ascetic type of attitude towards world comes in. Asceticism, as he mentioned in this book, at the beginning of the chapter, has no value. You just say that I want to keep aloof from this world. And this is some people actually choose ascetic life because they want more than what the people can gain in this world.

¶12 They want more and they know that they can gain. So they abstain from the minimum, to gain the maximum. And this is not actually the path of a mystic. A mystic never sets on this route for the sake of getting the maximum. Now, you do not for example, enjoy the life because you want to enjoy the pleasures of Jannah and therefore, you are restricting you asceticism. Of course, you get that, but this is not a path of a mystic. This is a path of an ascetic and then the reward is for that. The mystic once asceticism because this world diverting from. What if the soul is not ready? Well, when they move on, when they go further, they don't need to become ascetic.

¶13 So they don't need to abstain from pleasures of this world because they do not divert them anymore. At the beginning, when they are training this soul they need this. So, first is removing everything which is in the heart and will come between the traveller and the truth. This is the first aim of the riyadah. The second aim is to making nafsul ammara subdued to annafsul mutmainnah. So the second is to render the commanding soul obedient to the transgressor so that the power of imagination and that of the destination, that's waham or khayal as we call it will be attracted to the ideas proper to the .. Usually our nafs is ammara or muztariddah. The opposite of lawamah is muztaridah.

¶14 It is the nafs which is always going up and down, which is not tranquil which cannot hold down. Now, because we think about many different issues our imagination always works in different areas. We want different sorts of things. So our nafs is all the time muztaridah. All the time it is agitated. It cannot have peace and rest. And that's what causes us to do wrong things because there are lots of imaginations that come to our mind and we want those imaginations to be realized and our nafs would order us. Now, this riyadah training is there to somehow subdue this nafsul ammara to nafsul mutmainnah. A nafs which is completely reliant on Allah and is completely tranquil when it's faced with different areas of the life.

¶15 And then he says that the commanding soul becomes obedient to the tranquil soul, so that the power of imagination and the destination will be attracted to the ideas proper to … abandoning those ideas that are proper to the base things. And the third aim of riyadah is refining the soul to receive admonition and knowledge because unless the soul is refined, it cannot receive that type of knowledge which is given to the mystics. So, the third is to render the innermost thought sensitive to attention. Of course, it needs some explanation as I said, sensitivity to the knowledge which could come from that other world.

¶17 Ans: Yes, as I said we are a channel or canal towards Allah. It is for refining that channel so that we could receive knowledge.

¶18 Well, by doing this no one would become a mystic okay. This is just preparation. First the iradah should come and for the iradah to come you need to be a very good person. Then the riyadah should be there. Riyadah needs to abstain from evil things, trivial world and all these things to purify yourself and your mind and all these things so that you can set on the first stage of this journey. Now, what is the first stage of this journey? Then, he mentioned that of course these stations of the mystics are explained in many different numbers. Some people say a mystic has 9 ascensions. Some say they have 12 ascensions and some say there are 100 stations for a mystic to go to annihilation.

¶19 Some say there are 1000 stations and they divide 100 stations into 10 stations. Some say there are 7000 stations. I mean, this is something you can imagine lots and lots of things on the way. And some people say there are no stations. It's always just one step. You just decide to go to that and you go nothing else. However, this is a very nice classification, which is put forward by Ibne Sina about the stations of the mystics. He mentioned three ranks for the mystics each of which has one station. And he explained that type of progression from one station to another is very beautiful, very difficult to actually explain. If you go to the next chapter, chapter 9 “Remark Concerning the First Step In Conjunction”.

¶20 This conjunction means of course, will soon be going and arriving at Allah. So the first step towards that usool is moment what is called the waqt or awqat. They say the first thing that the Sufi mystic would have is not of course, a very long experience of reality or a very long experience of knowledge. There are just moments of light shining for them and then stopping. And of course depending how purified they are, these moments might be very little. And I'm sure I mean every human being would have some of these moments. All of you have had some of these moments in your life, sometimes these moments do not depend on your knowledge and purification.

¶21 They come from Allah and you feel some sense of closeness to god when those moments come. But they are instant. It might take one second, one minute or whatever they go away, okay. Now, for a person who have iradah and have gone through that riyadah these awqat happen more clearly, more frequently. However, it is just like seeing the thunderstorm with thunder light from behind the clouds. It just comes give you a shine and goes. And then how he explained is beautiful. Furthermore, if the will and the spiritual exercise that is iradah and riyadah bring the knower to a certain limit. He will encounter pleasurable stolen looks. Now this stolen looks very nice phrase that he uses “Qhalsa”.

¶22 It is just like when you simply look at something and take your eyes back. And usually especially in Farsi language, they use this for people who suddenly fall into some sort of ecstatic sensation; they say they are in Qhalsa. Qhalsa means to have a pleasure look of the reality. So he said these stolen looks come first. So no mystic at the beginning would come to that huge knowledge about Allah. And the reason is, the soul should get prepared gradually. The soul is not prepared. If you see the thunder light, the light of the thunder, not from behind the clouds, your eyes will burn, isn't it? So at the beginning, it comes from behind the clouds, the Mercy of Allah very smoothly brings peace to your heart, so that your heart would expand and become more capable of receiving all these.

¶23 So he says he will encounter pleasurable, older look at the light of the truth. Now, the light of the truth is a light which blinds on experience eyes. So they have to become experienced, it should come from behind the clouds. If you want to look at the sun, you cannot look at it just you cannot gaze at it. And if these looks are lightning, that shines over the knower and then turns away from him. Now in our experiences of these things we never know about it. It sometimes comes and go. So we don’t realise that. He says that if someone has the iradah and training, they know that these times are coming to them. And before they come and after they go the old time, all the time they are in agitation, in unrest.

¶24 As he puts it, of course, the translation here is a bit dodgy. He says .. looks out what they call moments, waqt or awqat. Every moment is surrounded by two ecstasies, an ecstasy called truth and an ecstasy over the passing away. Now here it's mentioned ecstasy, which is not a good translation. I was looking to the interpretation of Ayatullah Hassanzadeh about this. He also said ecstasy is not the right word for this because he says every moment is shrouded by wajhdun ilayh, a wajh which actually passes you have about it. Not this wajh in Arabic originally means hope means that. So, before this comes, the mystic is actually eager willing for this moment to come.

¶25 So, they are always senseless until it comes and when it comes of course, the sadness goes. What is the second is a minute or something like that and when it goes they make they are even sadder or even sadder because now that has passed and they have experienced it, to have experienced the pleasure and now, well it's gone. So, he says every moment for the mystic and this is one of the most excruciating stations of mystics. They get these lightning of truth coming and they go. They have no control over it whatsoever and every lightning which comes through make and confirms the faith in their heart even more and more and the faith increases their eagerness towards the truth increases and of course they have to have patience.

It is impossible for the heart to take it. So, it comes, it expands the heart a little bit, it goes now time for operation. So it's like an operation it comes very smoothly Allah deals with your heart if you want to seek. The whole point if you want to align that to operate it to heart if you want and if you prepare yourself we would do it.

¶27 So it says so there are ecstasies or sorrow over the passing away of it and before it comes and over after it goes. After that these overwhelming moments must gradually increase. If the knower persists in the spirituality so they have to continue with that riyadah and then they will become more frequent.

And this is when actually your heart is somehow fixed upon those that are fixed upon your heart by directing raised for your heart and this is the station they call it tawaqqul. So, the first is waqt, the second is tawaqqul. Tawaqqul is actually when it's the light penetrates through your hearts but whenever he catches a glimpse of a thing returns from that thing the side of sanctity remembering something of the latter is then overcome by a fainting. ¶34 Then comes the third step, the third degree which is called “Istifaad”.

He then overcomes by a fainting spell after that he always sees truth in everything. Now, this is somehow mixed with the third stage actually which is istifaad seeing some sort of light of truth in everything. Now, the istifaad means somehow to jump from your place. This is the meaning of istifaad. Now, at the beginning, when these lights come to you, when these experiences come, it makes you very excited.

¶37 Okay, so that if someone is beside you, they can recognize that you are now in a different route. You are being somehow under the spell of some sort of supernatural training or teaching or something, this is called istifaad. And whenever that light comes, it changes the whole attitude. This is the first stage of course. The first and second it is not that strong, that will change okay. But the third one, when you go to the third stage that is a bit stronger, the dosage is now increased in a way that sometimes if the affects your body dosage of that light which comes from Allah and when you go through all these, you will find out that it is all coming in a way that Allah is taking you smoothly by increasing the dosage of that light so that your heart can take it until the end is come in very measured portions are very measured subscriptions from Allah.

¶38 And this is how we have built these stations. On his way to this limit his veils are lifted up from him, and he ceases to be calm. This is istifaad. But the novice companion pays attention to the nose being provoked out of his stability. If this is spiritual exercises prolonged, he will not be provoked by the lifting up of any veil and will be guided to consider his experience. This comes later on. But now he's at the station, which these flows of light when they come, it moves them, changes the attitude and all these things. Now, then, the second rank comes. Up till here, first, there were just light coming at moments and going and then these lights became stronger so that even if he did not look into light and look into anything else, he would have seen that this is connected to that light.

¶39 And then he came to a station with the dosage of that light was increased so that when it came to the heart, it moved it. Now, the situation changed in the second rank of all these stations. The second rank is when after that moving, he gets tranquillity. And he's not anymore moved by those lights, which comes with sort of high voltage electricity coming to his heart. He's not moved that anymore. Here he says that … is the fourth step which effects on the soul of familiarity with the truth. Now, this is called “Inqilab”. Inqilab means turning upside down. Now he turns upside down, he becomes a medium with that world unfamiliar with gradually, he becomes very familiar.

¶40 So some medium that then those lights coming, rays coming, it’s not high voltage for him anymore, he is very familiar. So he says that, after that spiritual exercise carries into a point at which his moment is converted. Now here, this conversion is the meaning of inqilab actually which is mentioned by Ibne Sina here converted into tranquillity. Thus, that which is a stolen, those stolen looks becomes familiar. Now, he doesn't actually have to still look at that light, the light is very familiar to him now. And the lightning becomes a clear lane.

¶41 He acquired the stable knowledge of the truth as if this knowledge is a continuous accompany in which he delights in the rupture of the fruit. If he turns away from this knowledge, he will do so with loss and regrets because sometimes he has to do that, he has to do business to go to the world. So it's always loss and regret that he wants to come from that light into the ordinary world and we see otherwise his pleasure is that light. And that's why some people never get tired of worship, because they are at this stage; they are very familiar with it. It is reported from Owais ul Qarani. We talked about him before. He was waiting for night, all day.

¶42 And when night came, he said okay tonight is for ruku. So, we went to ruku from the beginning of the night until morning. Then the next night he said okay this night is for sajdah. So he went for sajdah the whole night. And someone told him don't you get tired this long night? I don't find very long night. It is very short. And then it's reported from him that he said, I would like the whole life, that'd be one night. And I would have somehow passed it by one prostration to Allah. This comes, of course, if we want to do if you want to do, we want to do 15 minutes of sajdah, all the limbs and arms and feet gets tired, fatigue, pain comes, you see because we are not familiar with it.

¶43 When they become familiar with that, what they do not feel any pain of body. The body is always subservience to the soul; it always is the case, okay. Now, if the soul is after pleasure, then the body will pain and of course, then it stands for prayer, the soul doesn't want it, the body gets tired. If the soul wants, the body never gets tired; it's subservient to the soul completely. And that's why we get tired very soon of worship. So at this time, when this inqilab comes, this conversion or turning upside down of the human personality comes, then you will become familiar with that and the body would somehow follow the soul and then comes “Taghalgul”.

¶44 It is, when you fall water on the tree and the water goes down, this is taghalgul. It somehow get into the whole soul of the mystic. This knowledge the soul would become some sort of knowledge in some sort of life. Now, since then, remark consent the fifth step, manifestations contrary to inner experience to further delving into knowledge that further delving into knowledge, is the explanation of taghalgul. Up to this point, he manifests what he undergoes but if he delves into this knowledge, there will be less manifestation of this experience thus he will be present, while the absence and the stationary while marching on. There is a very nice poetry which says have you ever heard about an absent person who's present and I have that confident patience, I am absent, but I'm present.

¶45 Now, this says that this person is absent from other people, he is actually delving into something else delving into the knowledge that Allah has given him but he's at the center of present living among other things. And his existence become like an absent person, who is present, is delving in other I mean they are accompanying people of this world with their body but their souls are clinging to it, to the creatures that are in the malaul aala, very close to Allah. This taghalgul is that station, now they don't care about things. They cannot pay attention to things actually because they're completely absent from it. So, what he said about this is crap up to this point, he manifest what he undergoes.

¶46 But if he delves into this knowledge, there will be less manifestation of experience but he will be present while being absent and stationary while marching on. Now, up to this point all these came to him without control. Although now he had control of himself, but he doesn't have control of bringing this light. At the sixth stage he gets control over he has it whenever he wants. So this is called “Mashiya” Mashiya means will, wanting. So, perhaps up to this point, this knowledge is facilitated for him only at times, but then he moves gradually until he attains it whenever he wishes. He has become a complete mystic. Now you might say okay, what's beyond this? But there are steps beyond this as well.

¶47 Now it has come to a station, which those lights are under his control, you can bring them to the heart, you can move into the world of the angels and all these issues with his own console. So you see the second rank started with that inqilab, conversion, becoming familiar with the other world and ends with mashiya. After becoming familiar, it's just like for example, you are familiar with some people, but you can only go to them when they invite you. You'd like very much to be with them, you have become familiar with this inqilab but you cannot go to them all the time. You only can go when they invite you. Now, this familiarity increases until it's like your own house, you go there whenever you want, you visit them whenever you wish.

¶48 So, the familiarity has increased, okay. So the second rank ends at this point. He has the mashiya console over the experiences, light coming to his heart. Then comes third rank, the first step of which is tatahareeq meaning moving up more towards your lord. The remark concerning the seventh step conjunction with a .. without even a wish. Here he had wished it and he has it. Now he moves up, then he advances beyond this rank so that his situation does not depend on a wish. Rather, whenever he notices one thing, he also notices another. It means that whenever he see something, you see the power of God behind it. This move and this is the station which is mentioned in the Quran very much that “Afalaa yanzuroona ilalibili kaifa khuliqat” 88:17 Do they not look at the Camels, how they are made?

¶49 It means that when you look at the camel, you have to see the power of God or they not see what is in the heavens and the earth? It means when you look at them if you are at this station, you immediately see God with them as Imam Ali (as) says I never have seen anything unless except that I saw God before and after it. So it’s the god that I see. Not these things, these things are just shrouded encompassed by that power of Allah that I always see. And this is not that very high quality of Imam Ali (as). This is just something which they have. These people have about seven stages of their movement.

¶50 He advances beyond this rank so that his intuition does not depend on his wish rather than ever he notices one thing he also notices another. You see, there's no wish anymore. Unwittingly, when they see something they see God. Even if this noticing is not for the purpose of consideration, they don't want to do. They are not paying attention to that accompanies they see. But it is available to him to move away from the world of falsehood to the world of truths. Remaining in the latter while ignorant move around him, then around all around him, but he himself is moving into the world of truth. If he is among the ignorant, he is not written one of them, written from those who are not ignorant.

¶51 And this is exactly what he wants to say. He lives among dangerous people but he's not ignorant anymore. He sees everything around him. This tatahareeq would move him up until when he looks into everything, especially when he looks into his heart he sees only God. He's only god that he sees. As he said he whenever he looks at everything, even he doesn't want to consider it but he sees God. So his heart becomes a reflection of Allah. Now is it a pleasure, isn’t it? To look into yourself, you see Allah, look into yourself you see God. And then you might go and say, I am god because you completely see God in yourself, you see the reflection of God in your heart.

¶52 Now, however, still there is a hesitation. Now, this hesitation doesn't mean that he has doubts or anything or he's hesitant about whether to see God or not, because he always sees God. But the hesitation is as it's explained here, becoming a replica of truth, while remaining aware of oneself is taraddud. If it causes from spiritual exercise to attainment of the truth, the innermost thoughts will become a polished mirror which he faces. Now, this innermost thought, of course, probably, translation of something which is called qalb or the heart will become a polished mirror with which he faces the site of the truth. The lofty pleasures are then poured on him because he feels God. He sees the word of God, he sees the wonders of God, he sees the power of God, knowledge of God and momentarily the pleasure comes into his heart.

¶53 And he's pleased with himself due to the traces of truth that these pleasures invoke, isn't it? I mean, if you come to such as station and say, how what a soul. What a fascinating thing Allah has given me, the soul that I have, which can reflect completely Allah in him. And this activation, of course, not selfish type of fascination, you're fascinated of the power that Allah has rested in your heart. You could somehow reflect completely, it can become the house of God. As we have, the heart of the momin is the Haram of Allah; this is where Allah resides actually. This is the meaning of it; it can completely, very transparently reflect God's attributes. So he is pleased with himself due to the traces of the truth that these treasures invoke.

¶54 To Him belongs a grant as a truth and a glance at himself, for his is still reluctant. Now he's still reluctant in the sense that he's reluctant to lead himself. He is very pleased with his own soul that has so refined. So he looks at Allah once, how close is he? How wonderful? And looks at his own soul and wonders how big in my soul that can reflect that. So he's still in taraddud, going to himself going to god, going to himself going to God. Of course, not in an arrogant way you remember this, this is completely different from our type of selfish look at own selves. He is wonder he is somehow fascinated by the type of nafs, so that Allah has given him.

¶55 So this is taraddud but this should move away. He shouldn't look at himself anymore because that is a pit fall. Now the ninth station, which he calls wusool meaning arriving and the mystics call it annihilation. It is when he doesn't look at himself anymore. He's not fascinated by himself and his soul anymore. So not that he perishes, not that the soul would go because if the soul goes away there's no reflection of Allah. It's all comes through the soul, but he doesn't look at his own soul anymore. He's completely fascinated by looking at Allah. And whenever he looks at the soul, he looks at it as a mirror, not as something which has value in itself.

¶56 You see, it's like, when you look into the mirror, usually, I mean, you can experience this a few days. In the morning, when you go and look into the mirror you never see the mirror. You never have attention to it. You just see yourself. But now you put very nice frame for mirror, every morning, you would look at the frame how nice and look at the mirror to see yourself as well. You see the mirror you see this yourself. But if you take this nice frame out or if you out an ordinary frame then again, you don't see the mirror. You only see yourself. Now, this wusool is like that. If you take that mirror, if you break that mirror of course, you're not going to see yourself, the mirror shouldn't be there and it’s not going to go away.

¶57 That mirror reflects you. The soul is not annihilated. It's not going anywhere. The only thing we had the explanation of Alexander Knysh will very nicely explain the concept of fanaa that there is no self-perception anymore. You do not perceive yourself. Not that there is no soul because if there is no soul, there is no reflection of God. There is no experience; no pleasure of having those experiences nothing. So this is the final station. Following this, he abandons himself completely. He doesn't come back to himself anymore. He's so much fascinated by Allah that he doesn’t come back to himself anymore. Thus he notices the sign of sanctity only. Sign of sanctity of course, is a translation of Janabal Quds.

¶58 Janabal Quds is referring to Allah because he's so holy. He is the direction of holiness. So he only notices the sign of sanctity, if he notices his self, he does so in as much as it notices the truth as a mirror and not in as much as it is ornamented with the pleasure of having the truth. You see the mystic looks at his own soul because he said, Oh, what pleasure comes to this when he looks at Allah. So he's fascinated with this. When he comes to the final stage, he doesn't look at it in this way anymore. If he looks at it, he looks at it as a mirror, that's all. All the pleasures go for seeing that picture, that image of God.

¶59 At this point, the arrival is realised. So now the mystics come to the final point of the first journey of the mystic world. If you remember, we talked about 4 journeys. This is the final part. Now what has happened, he has arrived at a stage where he does not see himself anymore, he does not fear anything else anymore. It's just God reflected into that mirror of the heart. Is this the end? No, that's just the beginning, isn’t it? Now he has to move and examine and find out about that thing which is reflected in the heart. Now he's completely devoid of everything else and pays attention to that. And that second journey, which is even, of course, more pleasurable and more difficult than this first journey would start that, was journeying through haqq with haqq going, traveling through truths with the truth.

¶60 Allah will take him into his own role showing him his asmah and siffat and everything the differences in these, how things are created by his ashma and siffat. He moves through that. Up till now, it was just to get rid of him, isn't it? As Hafiz mentions, the only veil between you and God is yourself. So get aside, go away. Let you arrive at Allah. When he arrives and of course the second journey starts.

¶61 Q5. Not Audible Ans: No, on the judgement day not everyone will see Allah. “Kallaaa innahum ‘ar Rabbihim yawma’izil lamah jooboon” 83:15 they are in veil from the Lord on that day. If they are in veil here, they are in veil there. “Wa man kaana fee haaziheee a'maa fahuwa fil aakhirati a'maa wa adallu sabeelaa” 17:72 whoever lived in this world as blind shall live as blind in the Life to Come. It’s the same thing.

¶62 Q6. Not Audible

¶63 Ans: For mominoon, who have not completed this journey here. It will be completed from them there. Of course the stations would be different. Some of them have completed this here who will be totally somewhere else and those who have not completed this here would be somewhere else but it will be completed for them somehow and they will look at Allah eventually. “Wa wujoohuy yauma-izin 'alaiha ghabar a” 80:40 the faces which look at their lord on that day.

¶64 Q7. Not Audible

¶65 Ans: Of course, everything is Allah’s mercy. No, that wrong. As we have in hadith that Allah’s mercy has 100 parts and only 1 part has been revealed to this world. 99 parts are reserved for yaumul akhirah so that people are moved towards Allah.

¶66 Q8. Not Audible

¶67 Ans: At all these stages, people are involved in society. There is this tendency that usually when the mystics move into this world they are not familiar whether we want to retreat from this life. However in Islam we are told that you shouldn’t do that. The prophets, imams and many great urafa in Islam they have not taught actually and it is somehow advisable to do both at the same time.

¶68 Q9. Not Audible

¶69 Ans: We know that the western world is a world of material life and pleasures. However it doesn’t mean that if someone really has that iradah and self-training, they couldn’t do it here. I don’t think the environment would matter very much. It is that irada that should come and when it comes then in any situation you do it. Like Prophet Musa for example was in the house of Firaun or Prophet Yusuf in that house of that azeez and they completely overcame there soul.

¶70 Wa sallahu ala mohammadin wa aale hittahereen
